questions.stem: Which of the following structures is part of the hepatoduodenal ligament?
questions.explanation: The hepatoduodenal ligament contains the portal triad: portal vein, hepatic artery proper, and common bile duct. The portal vein is the correct answer; the other options are not within this ligament.
questions.source: Basic surgical anatomy of the liver

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is part of the portal triad found in the hepatoduodenal ligament?
questions.explanation: The portal triad consists of the portal vein, hepatic artery proper, and common bile duct. The portal vein is the second option. The celiac trunk and superior mesenteric artery are separate arterial branches, and the common bile duct is the third option.
questions.source: Basic hepatic anatomy; portal triad definition

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man undergoes a laparotomy for a perforated duodenal ulcer. During the operation the surgeon notes that the duodenum is attached to the posterior abdominal wall by a thin, fibrous band that extends from the duodenum to the posterior abdominal wall. Which of the following structures is most likely responsible for this attachment?
questions.explanation: The duodenal plate (also called the retroperitoneal layer of the duodenum) is a thin, fibrous layer that attaches the duodenum to the posterior abdominal wall. The ligament of Treitz suspends the duodenojejunal flexure, the hepatoduodenal ligament contains the portal triad, and the lesser omentum connects the liver to the stomach and duodenum.
questions.source: Basic surgical anatomy of the duodenum

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a palpable mass in the left upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑defined lesion arising from the splenic hilum. Which of the following structures is most likely involved in the tumour’s vascular supply?
questions.explanation: The splenic hilum is supplied by the splenic artery, a branch of the celiac trunk. A mass in this region most commonly involves splenic vessels, making option B correct. The left gastric artery supplies the stomach, the pancreaticoduodenal arteries supply the pancreas and duodenum, and the inferior mesenteric artery supplies the distal colon – all anatomically distant from the splenic hilum.

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a large, firm, non‑mobile mass in the right upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑defined lesion arising from the hepatic dome and displacing the gallbladder inferiorly. Which of the following structures is most likely to be involved by the tumor?
questions.explanation: A mass at the hepatic dome that displaces the gallbladder inferiorly most commonly originates from the right hepatic lobe and therefore involves the right portal vein, which runs along the hepatic dome. The right hepatic vein lies posterior to the liver and is less likely to be involved in a dome‑based mass. The cystic duct and right hepatic artery are situated more inferiorly and anteriorly, making them less probable sites of involvement.
questions.source: Anatomy of the liver and biliary tree
